subject.title: Tool-error warnings fire on benign non-zero exits (no-match grep, recovered retries) since exit-code-based isToolResultError (#93228)

question: Should a later successful shell call with different arguments clear an earlier unresolved tool error, or should the fix remain limited to classifying benign read-only non-zero outcomes before warning policy runs?
rationale: The first option changes the integrity contract for genuine prior mutations, while the second is a narrower regression repair; source inspection and tests can implement either choice but cannot determine the intended warning policy alone.

options.title: Narrow read-only classification
options.body: Treat structured no-result exits from recognized read-only commands as non-errors while preserving unresolved warnings for failed mutating calls.

options.title: Broaden retry recovery
options.body: Allow a later successful call of the same tool to clear an earlier error even when its action fingerprint differs, accepting a greater risk of hiding an unrelated failed mutation.

recommendation.title: Narrow read-only classification
recommendation.body: Treat structured no-result exits from recognized read-only commands as non-errors while preserving unresolved warnings for failed mutating calls.

likelyOwner.reason: The reported regression is tied to the merged structured terminal-state change associated with this contributor.
